title: Next Permutation

concept.title: The smallest step up
body: To find the next arrangement in dictionary order: go from the right to the first position `i` with `a[i] < a[i + 1]`. Everything after `i` is in decreasing order, which is the largest arrangement of that tail, so `a[i]` must grow. Swap it with the **smallest element to its right that is bigger than it** (found from the right), then reverse the tail so that it becomes the smallest possible.

body.code:
i = n - 2
while i >= 0 and a[i] >= a[i + 1]: i -= 1
if i >= 0:
    j = n - 1
    while a[j] <= a[i]: j -= 1
    a[i], a[j] = a[j], a[i]
a[i + 1:] = reversed(a[i + 1:])

body: If there is no such `i`, the array is the last arrangement; reversing the whole array gives the first one (sorted increasingly).

statement: Given an array of `n` integers (duplicates are possible), print the next arrangement in dictionary (lexicographic) order, comparing the arrays element by element. If the array is already the largest arrangement, print the smallest one, i.e. the array sorted in increasing order.
outputFormat: Print the resulting array on one line.

examples.note: This is the last arrangement; the answer is the first one: 1 2 3.

hints: Find the last position `i` where `a[i] < a[i + 1]`.
Swap `a[i]` with the last element to the right of it that is larger than `a[i]`.

explanation: The tail after the pivot is in decreasing order. Swapping the pivot with the next larger element of the tail and then sorting the tail (by reversing it) gives the smallest larger arrangement.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

i = n - 2
while i >= 0 and a[i] >= a[i + 1]:
    i -= 1
if i >= 0:
    j = n - 1
    while a[j] <= a[i]:
        j -= 1
    a[i], a[j] = a[j], a[i]
a[i + 1:] = reversed(a[i + 1:])
print(*a)
